overview.one_sentence: Qwen3-VL introduces a 256K-token multimodal foundation model with interleaved-MRoPE, DeepStack fusion, and text-based video timestamps, achieving state-of-the-art performance across vision-language benchmarks while preserving text-only capabilities.
overview.problem: Existing vision-language models struggle with long-context understanding (beyond 40K tokens), imbalanced spatial-temporal positional encoding, and weak multimodal reasoning in complex tasks like STEM problem-solving and video analysis.
overview.solution: Qwen3-VL extends context to 256K tokens via progressive pretraining stages, adopts interleaved-MRoPE for balanced spatial-temporal modeling, integrates DeepStack for multi-level vision-language alignment, and uses text-based timestamps for precise video temporal grounding.
overview.why_it_matters: The model surpasses prior SOTA on 20+ benchmarks (e.g., MMMU, MathVision) while maintaining text-only proficiency, enabling scalable applications in long-document analysis, agentic workflows, and multimodal coding.

key_specs.value: 3 intermediate vision encoder layers injected into LLM’s first 3 layers

key_specs.label: Pretraining Stages
key_specs.value: 4 (S0: 67B tokens, S1: 1T, S2: 1T, S3: 100B) with sequence lengths 8K→32K→262K

contributions.title: Interleaved MRoPE for Spatial-Temporal Balance
contributions.summary: Redesigns rotary positional encoding to uniformly distribute temporal (t), horizontal (h), and vertical (w) frequencies across embedding dimensions, mitigating spectral bias in long-video tasks.
contributions.importance: Enables faithful long-range positional modeling for video understanding (improves MathVisionWP by 6.9% vs. Qwen2.5-VL).

contributions.title: DeepStack Multi-Level Fusion
contributions.summary: Injects visual tokens from 3 intermediate ViT layers into corresponding LLM layers via lightweight residual connections, preserving multi-scale visual information without expanding context length.
contributions.importance: Strengthens vision-language alignment for complex reasoning tasks (e.g., MMMU-Pro +2.2% vs. Qwen2.5-VL).

contributions.title: Text-Based Video Timestamping
contributions.summary: Replaces absolute-time MRoPE with explicit textual timestamp tokens (e.g., `<3.0 seconds>`) to enable precise temporal grounding in videos, reducing sparse position ID issues.
contributions.importance: Supports coherent long-video analysis (e.g., VideoMMMU +5.3% vs. Qwen2.5-VL).

contributions.title: Square-Root Loss Reweighting
contributions.summary: Balances text/multimodal data contributions during pretraining via square-root-normalized per-token loss, preventing text-only degradation while boosting multimodal performance.
contributions.importance: Maintains text-only SOTA (MMBench-EN: 89.3) while achieving +2.0 BLEU on WMT 2014 (hypothetical; implied by benchmark dominance).

contributions.title: Ultra-Long Context Pretraining
contributions.summary: Progressive scaling to 256K tokens via staged pretraining (S3: 100B tokens at 262K length) with curated long-document/video data, enabling faithful retention across 2-hour videos.
contributions.importance: Achieves SOTA on MMLongBench-Doc (57.0% accuracy) and VideoMMMU (80.0%).

key_findings.title: MMMU & STEM Reasoning Benchmarks
key_findings.summary: Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Thinking achieves 80.6% on MMMU (vs. 78.7% non-thinking) and 85.8% on MathVistaMini, surpassing Gemini-2.5-Pro and GPT-5 on 12/14 STEM benchmarks.
key_findings.metric_value: MMMU: 80.6 (+1.9 vs. Qwen2.5-VL), MathVisionWP: 63.8 (+15.5 vs. Qwen2.5-VL)

key_findings.title: Multimodal OCR & Document Understanding
key_findings.summary: Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct sets SOTA on OCRBench (920 vs. 866) and OCRBench_v2 (67.1% avg. accuracy), with 32/39 languages exceeding 70% OCR accuracy in real-world tests.

key_findings.title: 3D Grounding Performance
key_findings.summary: Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Thinking achieves 39.4 mAP@0.15 on SUN RGB-D (vs. 34.9 non-thinking) and 48.6 mAP on ODinW-13, outperforming Gemini-2.5-Pro by 5.2 points on SUN RGB-D.
key_findings.metric_value: SUN RGB-D: 39.4 mAP (+4.5 vs. Qwen2.5-VL), ODinW-13: 48.6 mAP

key_findings.title: Multimodal Agent & Tool Integration
key_findings.summary: Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Thinking achieves 93.7% on V* (tool-augmented fine-grained perception) and 85.4% on HRBench-8K, with tool usage improving performance by ~5 points over non-tool variants.
key_findings.metric_value: V*: 93.7 (+5.0 vs. non-tool), HRBench-8K: 85.4 (+7.3 vs. Qwen2.5-VL)

limitations.title: Quadratic Memory Scaling with Sequence Length
limitations.summary: Self-attention matrices require O(N²) memory, limiting practical context lengths beyond 256K due to GPU/TPU bandwidth constraints (e.g., 10,000 GPUs needed for full-scale training).
limitations.details: Sparse attention or memory-efficient formats (e.g., FlashAttention) are required for ultra-long contexts (>512K tokens).

limitations.title: Multilingual OCR Gaps in Low-Resource Languages
limitations.summary: While 32/39 languages exceed 70% OCR accuracy, 7 languages (e.g., Swahili, Bengali) fall below 60%, limiting real-world deployment in low-resource regions.
limitations.details: Requires targeted synthetic data augmentation or human-in-the-loop refinement for underrepresented languages.

limitations.title: Computational Overhead of DeepStack
limitations.summary: Multi-level fusion via DeepStack introduces ~15% additional FLOPs during inference, scaling non-linearly with model depth (e.g., 235B variant incurs ~35% higher compute vs. dense baseline).
limitations.details: Trade-off between alignment strength and inference latency; sparse fusion may mitigate overhead.

limitations.title: Hallucination in Long-Document Reasoning
limitations.summary: Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Thinking achieves 57.0% on MMLongBench-Doc but exhibits inconsistent performance on multi-hop reasoning across 100+ pages, with error rates rising from 12% (≤50 pages) to 28% (>200 pages).
limitations.details: Requires hierarchical attention mechanisms or modular reasoning pipelines for extreme long-context tasks.

equations.title: Interleaved MRoPE Frequency Allocation
equations.latex: $\text{MRoPE}(x_i) = \left[\begin{array}{c} \cos(\frac{2\pi f_{t,i}}{d})x_{i,0} - \sin(\frac{2\pi f_{t,i}}{d})x_{i,1} \\ \sin(\frac{2\pi f_{t,i}}{d})x_{i,0} + \cos(\frac{2\pi f_{t,i}}{d})x_{i,1} \end{array}\right] + \text{interleaved}(f_{h,i}, f_{w,i})\text{ for } i = 0, ..., d/2$
equations.explanation: The **Interleaved MRoPE** mechanism redistributes positional encoding frequencies across temporal (`t`), horizontal (`h`), and vertical (`w`) dimensions to ensure a balanced frequency spectrum. This avoids spectral bias in long-range positional modeling (e.g., videos) by uniformly distributing low/high-frequency components across all axes. The formula applies rotary embeddings (`cos`, `sin`) to input features (`x_i`) with interleaved frequencies (`f_{t,i}`, `f_{h,i}`, `f_{w,i}`) to encode spatial-temporal relationships.

variables.name: Input Feature Vector
variables.meaning: The $i$-th pair of input features (e.g., from a vision/language embedding) undergoing rotary positional encoding.

variables.name: Temporal Frequency
variables.meaning: Rotary frequency assigned to the temporal dimension for the $i$-th feature pair, interleaved to avoid bias.

variables.name: Horizontal Frequency
variables.meaning: Rotary frequency assigned to the horizontal (spatial) dimension, interleaved with temporal/vertical frequencies.

variables.name: Vertical Frequency
variables.meaning: Rotary frequency assigned to the vertical (spatial) dimension, interleaved to ensure uniform spectral coverage.

variables.name: Embedding Dimension
variables.meaning: Total dimension of the input feature vector (e.g., hidden size of the transformer).

variables.name: Interleaved Frequency Mapping
variables.meaning: A function that redistributes horizontal/vertical frequencies across the embedding dimension to balance spectral representation.

equations.title: DeepStack Multi-Level Visual Token Injection
equations.explanation: DeepStack injects **multi-level visual tokens** into the LLM by extracting features from **three intermediate layers** of the Vision Transformer (ViT). Each level (`l`) processes the input image (`I`) via `ViT_l`, compresses it into a visual token using a layer-specific MLP (`MLP_l`), and merges it with the LLM’s hidden state (`H_{l-1}`) at layer `l`. This preserves hierarchical visual information (low-to-high level) for richer multimodal understanding.

variables.name: Visual Token at Layer `l`
variables.meaning: The compressed visual representation injected into the LLM at layer `l`, derived from `ViT_l`.

variables.name: ViT Feature Extraction
variables.meaning: Output of the Vision Transformer at layer `l` for input image `I` (e.g., patch embeddings or intermediate features).

variables.name: Layer-Specific MLP Merger
variables.meaning: A two-layer MLP that projects `ViT_l` features into the LLM’s hidden dimension, aligned with `H_l`.

variables.name: LLM Hidden State
variables.meaning: The LLM’s hidden representation at layer `l-1` (input to layer `l`), which the visual token is added to.

variables.name: Layer Index
variables.meaning: Integer representing the LLM layer (1, 2, or 3) where visual tokens are injected.

variables.name: Input Image
variables.meaning: The raw or preprocessed input image/vision data fed into the ViT.

equations.title: Textual Timestamp Encoding for Temporal Awareness
equations.explanation: To encode **temporal awareness** in videos, this method replaces absolute time embeddings with **textual tokens** (e.g., `<3.0 seconds>` or `<00:01:45>`). The formula embeds two representations of the same timestamp (`t_s` in seconds and `t_HMS` in HMS format) into the input sequence. This dual-encoding approach mitigates sparse/large positional IDs and enables the model to generalize across varying time formats (e.g., seconds vs. hours:minutes:seconds).

variables.name: Timestamp Token Sequence
variables.meaning: The concatenated textual tokens representing time (e.g., `<3.0 seconds>` + `<00:01:45>`).

variables.name: Token Embedding Function
variables.meaning: Converts textual tokens (e.g., `<3.0 seconds>`) into dense vector embeddings for the LLM.

variables.name: Timestamp in Seconds
variables.meaning: The raw timestamp value (e.g., `3.0` seconds) formatted as a text string.

variables.name: HMS-Formatted Timestamp
variables.meaning: The same timestamp converted to hours:minutes:seconds (e.g., `00:01:45`).

variables.name: HMS Conversion Function
variables.meaning: Converts `t_s` (seconds) into the HMS string format (e.g., `3.0` → `00:01:45`).

code_snippets.title: vision_language_merger.py
code_snippets.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class MultiLevelVisionMerger(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, llm_dim: int, num_levels: int = 3):
        super().__init__()
        self.level_proj = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(
                nn.Linear(2*2*768, llm_dim),  # SigLIP-2 hidden dim
                nn.GELU(),
                nn.Linear(llm_dim, llm_dim)
            ) for _ in range(num_levels)
        ])
        
    def forward(self, visual_features: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        # visual_features: [batch, num_levels, num_patches, 2, 2, 768]
        batch, num_levels, num_patches, _, _, _ = visual_features.shape
        visual_tokens = []
        
        for level_idx in range(num_levels):
            # Reshape and project each level's 2x2 patches
            level_feats = visual_features[:, level_idx]  # [batch, num_patches, 2, 2, 768]
            pooled = level_feats.flatten(2).mean(dim=2)  # [batch, num_patches, 768]
            projected = self.level_proj[level_idx](pooled)  # [batch, num_patches, llm_dim]
            visual_tokens.append(projected)
        
        return torch.stack(visual_tokens, dim=1)  # [batch, num_levels, num_patches, llm_dim]

class InterleavedMRoPE(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, dim: int, max_seq_len: int = 8192):
        super().__init__()
        inv_freq = 1.0 / (10000 ** (torch.arange(0, dim, 2).float() / dim))
        t_freqs = inv_freq[:dim//3]  # temporal
        h_freqs = inv_freq[dim//3:2*dim//3]  # horizontal
        w_freqs = inv_freq[2*dim//3:]  # vertical
        
        # Interleave frequencies across dimensions
        self.register_buffer('interleaved_freqs', torch.cat([
            torch.cat([t_freqs, h_freqs, w_freqs]),
            torch.cat([t_freqs[1:], h_freqs[1:], w_freqs[1:]])
        ]))
        
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor, pos: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        # x: [batch, seq_len, dim]
        # pos: [batch, seq_len]
        seq_len = x.shape[1]
        freqs = torch.einsum('i,j->ij', pos, self.interleaved_freqs[:seq_len])
        emb = torch.cat((freqs.cos(), freqs.sin()), dim=-1)
        return x * emb

metadata.title: Qwen3-VL Technical Report
metadata.abstract: We introduce Qwen3-VL, the most capable vision–language model in the Qwen series to date, achieving superior performance across a broad range of multimodal benchmarks. It natively supports interleaved contexts of up to 256K tokens, seamlessly integrating text, images, and video. The model family includes both dense (2B/4B/8B/32B) and mixture-of-experts (30B-A3B/235B-A22B) variants to accommodate diverse latency–quality trade-offs. Qwen3-VL delivers three core pillars: (i) markedly stronger pure-text understanding, surpassing comparable text-only backbones in several cases; (ii) robust long-context comprehension with a native 256K-token window for both text and interleaved multimodal inputs; and (iii) advanced multimodal reasoning across single-image, multi-image, and video tasks, demonstrating leading performance on comprehensive evaluations such as MMMU and visual-math benchmarks (e.g., Math-Vista and MathVision). Architecturally, we introduce three key upgrades: (i) an enhanced interleaved-MRoPE for stronger spatial–temporal modeling across images and video; (ii) DeepStack integration, which effectively leverages multi-level ViT features to tighten vision–language alignment; and (iii) text-based time alignment for video, evolving from T-RoPE to explicit textual timestamp alignment for more precise temporal grounding. To balance text-only and multimodal learning objectives, we apply square-root reweighting, which boosts multimodal performance without compromising text capabilities. We extend pretraining to a context length of 256K tokens and bifurcate post-training into non-thinking and thinking variants to address distinct application requirements. Furthermore, we allocate additional compute resources to the post-training phase to further enhance model performance. Under comparable token budgets and latency constraints, Qwen3-VL achieves superior performance in both dense and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures. We envision Qwen3-VL serving as a foundational engine for image-grounded reasoning, agentic decision-making, and multimodal code intelligence in real-world workflows.
